marks.gloss_en: שנאמר וכסהו בעפר -- עפר לא נאמר אלא בעפר, מלמד שהשוחט צריך שיתן עפר למטה ועפר למעלה
והא בעי כסוי! וכי תימא דמכסו ליה -- והאמר רבי זירא אמר רב: השוחט צריך שיתן עפר למטה ועפר למעלה -- the blood of a bird hit in flight falls where no earth was put below
Rav: one who slaughters must put earth below and earth above [the blood]
חזינן גידפי דמיפרמי -- we see the feathers unravelled
דמזמין ליה לעפר דכולה פתקא -- he designates for himself the earth of the whole valley
תנינא אפילו כל שהוא -- the mishna's 'even any amount' is adduced as covering the cobbler's needle
לא, איזמל -- 'any amount' denotes the scalpel, not the cobbler's needle; the citation does not reach the needle
איזמל בהדיא קתני לה -- if 'any amount' already means scalpel, why does the mishna state scalpel explicitly?
פירושי קא מפרש -- the explicit scalpel clause explains what 'any amount' denotes
the mishna's phrase 'even any amount' refers to the scalpel; the later explicit scalpel clause explains the phrase
הכי נמי מסתברא -- if a cobbler's needle were valid under 'any amount', the larger scalpel clause would be superfluous
the scalpel clause is necessary to reject a decree against the hornless scalpel due to the horned one; it is not redundant even if the needle were valid
if the smaller cobbler's needle were valid, explicitly validating a scalpel would appear unnecessary
slaughter with a scalpel is valid when the scalpel has no side protrusions
slaughter with an ordinary needle is invalid because a needle pierces rather than cuts
R' Zeira: [the mishna's 'a full neck' means] a full neck and beyond the neck
שנאמר וזבחת ... ואכלת -- what you slaughter you eat; what slaughtered of itself, not
a knife fell and slaughtered: even though it slaughtered in its [normal] manner, [the slaughter] is invalid
טעמא דנפלה, הא הפילה הוא -- כשרה (kind svara under protest: a טעמא ... הא inference from the mishna's wording; the text has no דיקא נמי)
the reason is that it fell; but if he dropped it -- valid, even though he did not intend [to slaughter]
דתני אושעיא זעירא דמן חבריא: זרק סכין לנועצה בכותל והלכה ושחטה כדרכה -- רבי נתן מכשיר (kind svara: no support kind for a bare דתני citation)
[the mishna's clause holds that] we do not require intent for slaughter

[recalled:] of the mishna 'and all of them who slaughtered while others watch them -- their slaughter is valid', we said: who is the tanna for whom intent is not required? and Rava said: it is R' Natan
there [the deaf-mute, imbecile, minor], he intends cutting of some kind
here [the thrown knife], it comes from the force of a person of understanding
עון כרת התרת, איסור מיתה מיבעיא? -- forced immersion released her from a karet prohibition (her husband); a prohibition carrying death (teruma) should surely be released
Rav Nachman: בעלה חולין הוא, וחולין לא בעי כוונה -- the source differs: her husband is chullin, and chullin needs no intent (= p_baalah_chullin, p_chullin_lo_baei_kavana)
ומנא תימרא? דתנן: גל שנתלש ... טהורין; מאי לאו אדם דומיא דכלים -- as vessels have no intent, a person needs none (kind svara under protest: the marker is דתנן)
her husband is chullin
ממאי? דלמא ביושב ומצפה אימתי יתלש הגל, וכלים דומיא דאדם (= p_okimta_yoshev_umetzapeh); defended against מאי למימרא at 31b.2-3 (see necessities) -- a deflection cannot be defended in the schema
perhaps we are dealing with one who sits and waits for when the wave will be detached; and vessels are like a person -- a person intends for them
a niddah who was forced and immersed -- she is pure for her house
